title: Substitution Simplifies the Integrand
caption_md: The blue curve shows the original integrand $f(x)=2x\cos(x^2)$. The dashed orange curve shows the antiderivative $F(x)=\sin(x^2)$, found by substituting $u=x^2$. The shaded area under $f(x)$ from $0$ to $x$ equals $F(x)-F(0)=\sin(x^2)$. Drag $x$ to the right and watch the accumulated area track $\sin(x^2)$ exactly — this confirms that the substitution $u=x^2$ correctly "undoes" the chain rule.
